primary_workload: ntt_butterfly --benchmark: forward NTT (Cooley-Tukey) over Goldilocks prime for batch=512 rows of n=16384 elements on GPU; time the kernel only (CUDA events)

acceptable_targets.description: Any modification to solve.cu that removes the per-row sequential loop with cudaDeviceSynchronize and replaces it with a single 2D-grid launch covering all batch rows at once, achieving median <= 80ms while passing --verify

misdiagnosed_targets.note: mod_pow_dev() is called per-thread in butterfly_stage_kernel, which is indeed redundant arithmetic. However this is NOT the cause of the regression. The regression is the per-row sequential loop with cudaDeviceSynchronize that serializes batch=512 rows through (1 + log_n=14) sync points each, destroying GPU occupancy. Precomputing a twiddle table would yield a modest ~2x kernel arithmetic speedup but cannot reach the 80ms threshold without removing the sync loop.

regression_pattern: per-row sequential loop with cudaDeviceSynchronize (progress-monitoring regression)
misleading_concept: redundant per-thread twiddle factor recomputation via mod_pow_dev()
misleading_counterfactual: Precomputing twiddle factors into a device table reduces arithmetic per butterfly but the dominant cost is (512 rows) x (1+14 stages) x cudaDeviceSynchronize = 7680 host-GPU round trips. Without removing the sync loop, no twiddle optimization can reach 80ms.
